name: code_change_task
system_prompt: You are an autonomous software-engineering agent working inside a service repository. A bug has been reported. Investigate by reading and searching code, inspecting the current diff, and running the tests, then form a hypothesis about the root cause. Reason step by step, prefer read-only exploration, and produce a concise summary of the root cause and the change that is needed.

symptom: a race in the cache layer

tool_descriptions.list_dir: List the entries (files and subdirectories) under a directory path in the repository, optionally recursing to a given depth. Use this first when you are not yet sure where the relevant code lives, to get oriented in an unfamiliar part of the tree before reading specific files. Returns each entry's name, size, and last-modified time, and marks directories distinctly from files so you can decide where to look next without reading file contents yet.
tool_descriptions.read_file: Read a file from the repository and return its contents as numbered source lines, optionally restricted to a start/end line range for a large file. Use this once you know (from list_dir, grep_code, or find_symbol) which file is relevant, to inspect the actual implementation rather than guessing at it. Line numbers in the output let you reference exact locations precisely in later edit_file or apply_patch calls, and in your final summary of the root cause.
tool_descriptions.grep_code: Search the repository source for a regex or literal pattern, optionally scoped to a specific file or directory, and return matching lines with path:lineno prefixes. Use this to find every call site of a symbol, every place a string or error message appears, or to confirm a hypothesis about where a bug originates before committing to reading a specific file in full. A narrow, specific pattern surfaces the relevant lines faster than a broad one that returns many unrelated matches.
tool_descriptions.find_symbol: Locate the definition of a function, class, or method symbol by name and return its defining file, line number, full signature, and the call sites that reference it elsewhere in the repository. Use this instead of grep_code when you already know the exact symbol name and want its definition plus every caller in one call, which is the fastest way to assess blast radius before changing a shared function's behavior or signature.
tool_descriptions.git_diff: Show the current uncommitted working-tree changes as a unified diff, optionally scoped to a path and optionally limited to staged changes. This is a read-only inspection of edits already made -- it does not create or discard any change. Use it to confirm exactly what has been modified so far in the session, to sanity-check an edit_file or apply_patch result, or to remind yourself of prior progress after a long tool loop.
tool_descriptions.run_tests: Run the test suite, optionally filtered to a specific test id or file, and return the runner's summary along with the full traceback for any failure. Use this both to reproduce a reported bug as a failing test before touching any code, and again after making a change to confirm the fix actually resolves the failure without breaking other tests. Prefer filtering to the relevant test file while iterating, and run the full suite once before concluding.
tool_descriptions.run_command: Run a read-only shell command in the repository root -- a build, lint, type-check, or `git log` -- and return the combined stdout/stderr along with the process exit code. Use this for checks that are not covered by a more specific tool, such as confirming a lint rule fires on a line before editing it, or checking recent commit history for context on why a piece of code looks the way it does. This tool is restricted to non-mutating commands.
tool_descriptions.edit_file: Apply a precise in-place edit to a file by replacing one exact occurrence of old_string with new_string, and return the resulting unified diff of the change. Use this for a small, targeted fix once you have located the exact lines to change via read_file or find_symbol -- old_string must match the existing file content exactly, including whitespace, or the edit will fail rather than silently applying to the wrong location.
tool_descriptions.write_file: Write a file with the given contents, creating it if it does not exist or overwriting it entirely if it does, and return the number of bytes written along with a diff against the previous version. Use this for a new file, or for a rewrite so extensive that a series of targeted edit_file replacements would be less clear than replacing the whole file at once. Prefer edit_file for small, localized changes to an existing file.
tool_descriptions.apply_patch: Apply a unified-diff patch to the working tree in one call and return which files and hunks were changed, or which hunks were rejected if the patch no longer matches the current file contents. Use this when you already have a multi-file or multi-hunk diff prepared -- for example a patch drafted from a git_diff of a similar prior fix -- rather than replaying the same set of edits one edit_file call at a time.

depth.description: How many levels deep to recurse.

pattern.description: Regex or literal pattern to search for.

path.description: File or directory to scope the search to.
Optional path to scope the diff to.

staged.description: Show staged changes instead of working tree.

test_path.description: Optional test id/node to filter to (e.g. tests/test_x.py::test_y).

command.description: Shell command to run in the repo root.
